description: Silent zero-work success that CLOBBERS the committed baseline artifact this merge exists to land. UPLOADS is a module-level hardcoded operator-laptop path ('/Volumes/Butter/WP/vlm/app/public/wp-content/uploads') with no flag and no env override, and REPORT_JSON/REPORT_MD resolve to docs/tasks/vlm/bakeoff-results/vlm-baseline-descriptions-20260716.{json,md} — the exact 464KB/156KB files this branch commits. On any machine without that volume mounted, every row fails p.exists(), todo==[], the loop never runs, and the finally: block still calls _write_report(), which reads the GITIGNORED out/*.jsonl (absent) and unconditionally overwrites the committed durable results with an empty report — then prints 'done.' and returns 0. Canon AGT-10 (degrade loudly) and RLSE-05 (silent failure is the worst failure): a gate instrument that reports success on zero work is a false green. Cross-slice inconsistency is the tell — florence_describe.py, authored in the same branch for the same job, correctly takes --images-dir/--tsv/--out-jsonl with env fallbacks and hard-errors via parser.error() when they are absent. Also rg-006 (documented commands must run as written). Fix: parameterize UPLOADS/ATTACH_TSV/OUT paths like florence_describe.py, and refuse to write the report when rows==[] but the JSONL/corpus was expected non-empty.
fix: Add --uploads/--tsv/--out flags with env fallbacks (mirror florence_describe.main); guard _write_report against writing an empty report over an existing non-empty one.

description: The caption and face anchor generators share one global journal name (_PROMOTE_JOURNAL='.vlm-anchor-promote.journal') and one stage prefix (_PROMOTE_STAGE_PREFIX='.vlm-promote-stage-') and both write into the same docs/tasks/vlm/bakeoff-results/ directory. A caption promote therefore discovers and 'recovers' a journal left by an interrupted FACE promote, installing face artifacts under caption authority (and vice versa). Impact: cross-generator artifact installation with no type check — the recovery path actively corrupts the freeze set it is meant to protect.
fix: Namespace the journal and stage prefix per generator (e.g. .vlm-anchor-promote.caption.journal) and have _recover_promote assert the journal's declared generator matches the caller before acting.

description: The B_eyewear clustered +/-10pp floor is 48 in the scope doc and 49 in the test, because the two artifacts size DIFFERENT populations -- the same AUDIT-11 defect closed as BR-29, one cell down. Found by R10, COORDINATOR-VERIFIED at e8dece4a: running the 80 B_eyewear entries of benchmarks/manifests/fir12-selection-v1.json through shipped project_frame_psu_image_counts gives 55 PSUs, sum(m)=80 (= N_h exactly), sum(m^2)=168, so the genuine frame-PSU Kish a = 168/80 = 2.1 and size_for_margin(margin=0.10, population=80, cluster_size=2.1, icc=0.2).n == 48, which is what the doc publishes. The test module instead hardcodes B_EYEWEAR_KISH_A = 2.36 (= 177/75, from project_strata_subject_image_counts over 47 OVERLAPPING labeled subjects whose sum(m)=75 != 80) and asserts 49 in four places (lines ~547, 556, 572, 577). An a computed over a labeled-membership join is being applied to a larger frame -- exactly the partition violation AUDIT-11 forbids. Downstream, allocate(n=84, precision_floors={B_eyewear: 0.10}, cluster_params=...) differs by one image between the two: B=48/E_clean=26 vs B=49/E_clean=25. Whole-frame planning n=198 is consistent and is NOT this cell. R10's mutant m3 also shows the doc's B cell is unguarded: setting the planning fence to cluster_size=2.36 (which computes 49) while leaving the comment '# 48' left all three sampling tests GREEN -- distinct from BR-31/BR-32, which are about the missing comment assertion, not this value clash. AUDIT-11, AUDIT-09, AUDIT-10.

CANON EVAL-DESIGN REVIEW (rv-strata). The committed corpus has NO populated difficulty, domain, cohort or capture-condition strata, so those cells CANNOT gate. CONFIRMED by direct count on the seed manifest: 37 entries with {'domain': 0, 'difficulty': 0, 'tags': 0, 'demographic_cohort': 0, 'face_boxes': 0}. domain and difficulty exist only as OPTIONAL schema fields; difficulty has no production metric or gate consumer at all, and domain is consumed by threshold calibration, not by the final report gate. Caption scoring produces no domain or difficulty rows whatsoever; face demographic results are directional and omitted from gate_proposal. Scenario: 100 faces from condition A pass and one from condition B fails — aggregate 99.0%, cohort B never enters the proposal, worst cell 0%. Canon EVAL-04 ('report and floor metrics per critical slice'), FAIR-01 ('gate on the worst cohort, not the mean'), FAIR-05 ('treat instrumentation and environment as first-class factors' — the entry schema has NO hardware, device, lighting or environment field). NOTE this is the FIR-12-side twin of VLM-6-CAN-10. Fix: populate subject, cohort, domain, difficulty, capture device, lighting, environment and session fields; define minimum cell sizes; gate the WORST production-critical cell; make missing mandatory strata a manifest validation error for ship-gate corpora.

L373 asserts identity-level ICC understates ρ, identity-level m *overstates* occasion m, "the two biases do not cancel," and the note "carries the DEFF under both readings as a bracket." In `DEFF = 1+(m−1)ρ` (L104) the two errors enter with opposite signs, so both "readings" can err the same way — and under the fallback the store yields only one `(m_id, ρ_id)` pair, so there are not two computable readings that sandwich the truth. L103 states the opposite m direction ("identity is a *lower bound* proxy for occasion; true m is larger"). L67/L88/L102 ban identity as a resampling/cluster unit because identity clusters do not partition (14+3 overlap, 108 in none) and say identity "is not the fallback" — L373 step (2) and L534 make it the fallback anyway. With 113/150 entries CDN-shaped (L331), EXIF/session recovery fails on most rows, so this fallback is the central path, not an edge; and no proof step checks the claimed bias signs against the rows where the EXIF key *does* recover a grouping (L534). Impact: the 3.1 multiplier behind 905/6,300 and the Slice 6 floors (L461, L566) is not known to bound the estimand DEFF, and capture spend moves with the sign of an unresolved contradiction.
Sources: G1-4, G3-5, G3-13

A PUBLISHED protocol disclosure was rewritten to name an internal Python symbol instead of the mathematical rule it discloses. SYNTHETIC_OCCLUSION_PROTOCOL_DISCLOSURES is not a comment — report.py:162 splices it into the published disclosure list with `*SYNTHETIC_OCCLUSION_PROTOCOL_DISCLOSURES`, alongside peers written as self-contained, reader-evaluable prose ('fit-phase galleries are restricted to fit-fold identities (CAL-07) while read-phase LOO galleries span the full matched corpus — tau_k is selected against a lower-cardinality gallery...'). Lane P1a changed 'occlusion recovery uses open-set threshold (s_max >= tau), not closed-set argmax' to '...(accept_predicate.accepts), not closed-set argmax'. An external reader of an eval report cannot evaluate `accept_predicate.accepts`; they CAN evaluate `s_max >= tau`. A disclosure exists so a reader can reconstruct the protocol WITHOUT reading the source, so pointing it at a source symbol defeats its only purpose. Coordinator-caused: my lane brief said 'update the two prose comments in synthetic_occlusion (around lines 9 and 84)' — line 84 is a published disclosure, not a comment, and the instruction was wrong for that site. The module-docstring change at line 9 IS a comment and is fine. Canon AUDIT-13, OBS-08.
fix: Restore the mathematical statement in the published disclosure: 'occlusion recovery uses open-set threshold (s_max >= tau), not closed-set argmax'. If a source pointer is wanted for maintainers, append it rather than substituting it — the inequality must survive in the published text. Leave the module-docstring edit at line 9 as-is; that one is genuinely a comment.

[GAP] The installer derives the target slice from the effective UID but writes under `/etc/systemd/system`, which requires root. Running it as the target user cannot write the drop-in; running it with `sudo` changes the UID to 0 and configures `user-0.slice` instead of the gate user's slice. The tests avoid this production permission and identity path via a temporary override.

description: Operator merge-only curation freezes buffalo false-JOINS into ground truth. The workflow (buffalo detect -> embed -> cluster -> human merges over-splits) is proposal-limited adjudication: humans can fix over-segmentation but a merge-only pass never systematically splits a buffalo cluster containing two people. Consequence: GT is a human COARSENING of buffalo's own partition on buffalo's own detections, so buffalo's false_split 0.065 vs candidate 0.351 (5.4x) is preferentially optimistic for the incumbent and is not a safe independent comparison. Identity labels are better than raw auto-cluster IDs; they are NOT 'better ground truth than the boxes' (category error - boxes remain 369/375 = 98.4% detector-minted).

FIR-11 releases FIR-7's burn-after-use K=3 seal at the wrong slice. plan:191 states 'FIR-7's Slice 0a baseline is re-drawn on the post-Slice-2 manifest', but Slice 2 ships only schema, lineage and the split; the non-circular labels and the bias bound arrive in Slice 3 (plan:190 'DIRECTIONAL is the ceiling until Slice 3 publishes the bias bound'). The seal therefore still lands on merge-only buffalo truth. The exec summary (:198) cites this exact ordering as the MITIGATION for its number-one program risk, so the stated mitigation does not mitigate.
fix: Move the FIR-7 re-draw to post-Slice-3, or state explicitly that the seal is provisional and re-drawable.

description: Coverage lost while adding coverage. `_cmd_score` builds `json_doc`/`md_doc` at line 654 and writes them to disk at 664-665. `_check_score_determinism_cross_process` then rebuilds its own `base_json`/`base_md` from the persisted record and compares only the three subprocesses against that new baseline. Nothing ever compares `base_json` to `json_doc`. The old same-process check did exactly that comparison, so intra-process nondeterminism between two `build_reports` calls (mutable module state, memoization, accumulator reuse) was caught before and is invisible now. Worse, the artifact actually written to disk is no longer the artifact the determinism check certified.
fix: After the helper's baseline build, also assert `base_json == json_doc and base_md == md_doc` with its own distinct message (e.g. `determinism check FAILED: in-process re-score differs from the written report`). Pass the already-built docs into the helper rather than discarding them. Prove RED by making build_reports return a differing second result.

description: README contract table omits not_ready. Line 295 documents verdict as `pass | fail | pass_ungated`, and the reasons table omits category-vacuity entirely, so an operator reading the docs can still treat pass as the only non-fail outcome.

description: sha-guard:ignore blanks every token on its line. The implementation is `if _IGNORE_MARKER in line: continue`, so 'commit deadbee and also cafebab sha-guard:ignore' exits 0 with both tokens unchecked. It is a documented escape, but a one-marker-wide door for multi-SHA lines.
fix: Scope the ignore to the nearest token, or require the marker to immediately follow the foreign token.

description: [TEST-07] The new guard's sleep_ms UDF is registered on one aiosqlite connection obtained via engine.connect(), then relied upon from a separate sf() checkout. Reviewer confirmed the sequential path currently reuses the same connection (matching aiosqlite_id, SELECT sleep_ms(1) succeeded) but that is pool LIFO/lazy luck, not a guarantee (pool_size=5). Probe with the UDF connection held open: sf() gets a different connection, the query raises 'no such function: sleep_ms', 'started' never sets, and the test dies at line 158 with a BARE TimeoutError carrying no message. Not a silent pass — a misleading failure that points a reader at the UDF timing instead of at connection identity. Same behaviour under NullPool.
fix: Pin the guard to a single connection explicitly (register the UDF on the connection the query runs on, or use a connect event listener so every pooled connection carries sleep_ms), and give the wait_for a message so a UDF miss is self-describing.

description: [local claude lens L][TEST-15] (same sites as VLM6-RV10-Q2-01; extra angle) The two round-9 'cannot read manifest' OSError guards (~:2718-2725, ~:2748-2755) are unreachable via the CLI: load_manifest (:2692) already reads args.manifest and raises ManifestError -> named exit 1 for chmod-000 / directory manifests, so the guards are TOCTOU-only, exit-code 2 contract unobservable, and `git grep 'cannot read manifest' -- scene/tests/` is empty. TEST-15 survivor, verified: changing flattenError's recursive call from flattenError(value.cause, false) to (…, true) keeps all 11 logger tests green. The test 'flattens Error cause one level without stack' builds only a single nested TypeError, which has no cause of its own, so one-level and two-level flattening produce identical output. The stated invariant of this module is 'the default docker build target must stay torch-free' (docstring line 1), but every gate in the slice implements it as 'does not resolve the project vlm EXTRA'. A grep of tests/deploy and tests/unit/test_fir_release_gates.py shows no assertion on torch absence in the default image path at all (the only torch tests are in test_vlm_lock_is_cpu_only.py, which checks the lock's wheel flavour, not the default image). The gate therefore enforces one spelling of the contamination, not the property.
fix: Add a direct contamination gate on the default image path: assert no install fragment in builder/runtime effective bodies names torch/transformers/nvidia-/triton, and/or resolve the effective installed dependency set from uv.lock for the synced extras and assert torch is absent.

description: [SECD-02] Host GPU reaper reads container-writable describe-load.json without a size bound and follows symlinks. Attacker: Code execution in an api container (writer of /run/acx-write/<env>). A non-regular or oversized publication can hang or exhaust the host lifecycle process. The GPU self-stop watchdog limits the cost impact. Evidence: load_source.py:414-417 read_text has no bound, unlike _read_bounded at :275-278/551-563; EXECUTED probe: symlinked 8 MiB file accepted as trustworthy, peak allocation about 16 MB against the 1 MiB fence budget.
fix: Open with O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK, require S_ISREG, and reuse _read_bounded.

description: The integrity gate is self-referential and therefore provides no protection against the threat it is documented to cover. MANIFEST_FILENAME lives INSIDE the snapshot directory (verify_vlm_cache.py:57-58, 228) on the same bind mount as the payload it certifies, and is unsigned and unpinned — no digest of the manifest is baked into the image or the repo. Concrete failure: an attacker (or any process) with write access to the host path behind `${ACX_MODELS_PATH}` swaps `modeling_florence2.py` for a payload AND rewrites `acx-vlm-cache.manifest.json` with the new sha256 in the same operation; verify_snapshot passes cleanly and `trust_remote_code=True` then execs the payload as the acx user with DB credentials in the environment. The container-side `:ro` flag is irrelevant — it constrains the container, not the host or any sibling container mounting the same path. What the gate actually detects is truncated/partial/hand-copied seeds and accidental drift, which is worthwhile, but README:801-808 and the docstring at verify_vlm_cache.py:31-37 sell it as the SEC-13 anti-tamper control ('possible cache tamper', 'the RB-02 attack surface: an attacker ADDS a .py'), which overstates it.
fix: Store the manifest OUTSIDE the mounted cache — bake a detached `acx-vlm-cache.sha256` (or just the manifest's own sha256) into the image at build time via a build ARG, and have the gate verify the on-mount manifest against that baked digest before trusting it. Until then, downgrade the SEC-13 language in README:801-808, the module docstring and Dockerfile:166-171 from 'cache tamper' to 'corruption/partial-copy detection' and state the residual risk explicitly.

description: The provenance guard fails wholesale in a shallow clone with no documented precondition. It resolves stamps only against the local object database; in the codex reviewer's shallow mirror (`git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` = true) it reported ALL 57 harvested stamps MISSING and exited 1. Neither scripts/README.md:22-35 nor the script itself advertises a full-history requirement. This is a live operational risk rather than a theoretical one: CI checkouts are shallow by default, and this repo's own offload lanes run against shallow mirrors on the VM -- so the guard reports total provenance failure in exactly the environments it is meant to protect. The failure mode is worse than a false negative: an operator seeing 57/57 MISSING is being invited to conclude the guard is broken and loosen it, which is how a real missing stamp later slips through. [rg-006][PROV-01]
fix: Detect a shallow repository and either fail with an explicit 'cannot verify: shallow clone, run with --unshallow' message or skip resolution with a loud non-green status. Never report 'MISSING' for a SHA the local ODB simply cannot see.

description: [ANTIPATTERN] (wave 4c lane review, verified on beefed28a) acquire_grok_lane_lock returns success without holding any lock when .lane-lock-<key> is absent (l366), and never re-checks that the path still names the flocked inode before deletion. A materializer re-creating the same key can create and lock a fresh inode while the reaper is mid-deletion, so mutual exclusion is not a stable boundary; the snapshot gate protects the checkout's git state but not the lease/venv siblings (DDIA ch.8: a lock is only a lock if both writers cooperate on the same inode). Note the tension with retired L-09, which removed create semantics because the lock file outlived the sandbox; H-07 now retains the lock path anyway, so that objection no longer holds and the L-09 test case must be updated deliberately, not silently reversed.
fix: Open the lock with create semantics (exec 8>>"$lane_lock") and flock -n it in every case; before rm and before sibling cleanup verify [[ "$lane_lock" -ef /dev/fd/8 ]] and skip with 'lane lock replaced; skipped' otherwise. Update the L-09 case to assert the lock file is created-and-retained. Adversarial test: lock absent at start, materializer creates+locks the path during the final deletion window; assert lease/venv survive.

description: statusLine checks blockedReason before state.status, and the panel is never remounted on 'Reset practice' (GuidedDescriptionReview receives resetVersion as a prop, not as a key). Sequence: run a live description to READY, then press Reset practice -> resetGuidedScenario() puts every identity back to UNCONFIRMED -> blockedReason becomes 'no_faces_decided' -> the status line flips to 'Decide each face match first. Then you can describe this photo live.' while state.text is untouched, so the previous run's live sentence stays on screen in the blockquote underneath a status line saying no run is possible. Mid-run reset is worse: the reducer deliberately keeps the waiting status (liveDescription.ts:151-153) so the poll continues and, on completion, the fresh live sentence is rendered under the same 'Decide each face match first' copy.
fix: Clear the run when the gate closes (dispatch a reset that nulls text on the blocked transition) and/or render the blocked copy only when state.status is BLOCKED, so a terminal result is never shown under a blocked status line.

description: The conflict check ignores the image bytes, so a same-key/different-image submit silently replays the wrong run. The comparison covers media_ids + recognition_enabled only, and the replay returns at line 347 before _read_image_parts at 349, so the server structurally cannot compare what it is describing. Verified by execution: two submits with key K and media_ids [70] but different PNG bytes both return 202 with the same run_id; the second image is never described and the caller receives descriptions of the first image attributed to the second asset. Wrong alt text on the product's only output. rg-015 (the 409 claims payload equivalence it never established) and API-02.

description: OBS-08. `_printable_path`'s fallback only recovers a true filename when the underlying bytes are valid UTF-8. For a non-UTF-8 filename (latin-1 caf\xe9 on the Linux gate host) it emits `run-caf\\xe9-report.md` -- literally the nonexistent path RV13-L-01 was raised against -- and that output is byte-identical to a real file whose name contains the six ASCII characters backslash-x-e-9, so stdout is ambiguous and not machine-consumable. Verified: in='run-caf\udce9-report.md' -> out='run-caf\\xe9-report.md'; in='run-caf\\xe9-report.md' (literal) -> same output. The docstring itself concedes the escape is the lie yet the fallback returns exactly that.
fix: On the fallback branch emit the raw bytes to sys.stdout.buffer (or an explicitly flagged unrepresentable form) instead of a lossy backslashreplace string, so the printed token is always the real path or visibly marked as unrepresentable.

TEST-15 MUTATION TABLE: several regression tests have NO scorer-semantic kill power, and the main caption oracle is currently RED. CONFIRMED. Named mutants with no killer: `_fkre` 84.6→84.7 does NOT red its direct test (it asserts only a broad theoretical range) and depends entirely on the currently-broken caption snapshot; `_index_run` calls default 1→0 has NO assertion at all; fusion's handwritten manifest digest has no canonical-digest test (the current mismatch proves the hole); test_tokens_label_integer_zero_does_not_crash says in its own text that it has 'No kill power'; runner/report wiring tests never invoke caption scoring, so NO scoring edit can turn them red. description: Rescued from remote review lane ocirv-1-rev-res pass 2, EXECUTED on the gate VM. The catch-all `*ServiceError*` branch classifies EVERY OCI service response as vault_unreachable and prints a hint telling the operator the failure is transient and to check egress. The lane fed representative OCI 400 InvalidParameter and 409 Conflict payloads to ocir_classify_login_failure; both returned vault_unreachable with the retry/egress hint, indistinguishable from a genuine 429 or 500. So a malformed request or a conflicting vault state -- neither of which will ever succeed on retry -- is presented as a transient network problem, and the operator retries a deploy-blocking operation indefinitely instead of fixing the request. This sharpens the general misrouting recorded as OCIRV-1-S-05: the specific defect here is the retryable/terminal distinction being erased, which is the distinction that determines whether waiting is a valid strategy. Canon: RES-03, RES-13, DIAG-01, Release It! ch-5.

[GAP] A1 specifies leases that survive 503 responses, renew on retries, aggregate while unexpired, and expire abandoned demand, but it never defines the terminal transition for successful completion, cancellation, or permanent failure. Because has_work consumes unexpired leases, implementations may either leave completed operations asserting GPU demand until L or release them early and break retry guarantees; the listed tests do not cover terminal cleanup.

description: [GAP] Schema description claims the same shape family as GET /recognition/clusters/{cluster_id}/roster-candidates, but the envelope is only cluster_id + candidates (additionalProperties: false). roster-candidates-response requires model_id, embedding_model, computed_at, probe_face_count, reference_face_count, quality_flag, and thresholds, and forbids showing Strong when quality_flag is not ok. The task plan also says reuse list_roster_candidates, which emits those fields, while identity-merge.md defines a different ranker: max(centroid cosine, latest pending ClusterMergeSuggestion similarity). The new route cannot both reuse that path and match this thinner schema; PersonMergeDialog step 2 has no quality_flag with which to cap bands. There is also no top_k/limit, unlike roster-candidates.

description: [ANTIPATTERN] The smoke test hardcodes gpu_qwen30b and Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct instead of deriving the configured profile and model from the deployment/health contract. The valid gpu_qwen30b_ensemble profile shares the model but has a different profile value, so a supported deployment can be falsely rejected.
fix: Resolve the expected profile and model from the configured deployment or returned health payload and remove raw model/profile literals from the smoke test.

description: [GAP] The 'production markers not flipped' lock is mostly tautological. test_evidence_schema_is_complete only asserts JSON production_unverified_markers_flipped is False. test_documented_contract_is_not_treated_as_measurement pins declared_unverified_alignment_template_id and that the JSON note contains 'UNVERIFIED', but does not compare declared_unverified_input_scale, declared_unverified_channel_order, or declared_unverified_output_l2_normalized to MODEL_MANIFEST['auraface'].preprocessing, nor publisher_model_card.revision to AURAFACE_REVISION, nor provenance.py source UNVERIFIED comments (the check already used by test_auraface_preprocessing_stays_unverified). If the live unverified contract changes, this measurement record still passes.
fix: Bind those declared_* fields to MODEL_MANIFEST['auraface'].preprocessing (input_scale 1.0/127.5, channel_order RGB, output_l2_normalized True, alignment_template_id), pin publisher revision to AURAFACE_REVISION, and assert provenance.py still contains the UNVERIFIED comments rather than trusting the JSON boolean.

description: Dormant service raises an error toast. failedToastMessage maps ACTIVITY_REASON.GPU_STATUS_UNAVAILABLE to 'Description Service status unavailable' (gpuStatePresentation.ts:66), and GpuTierStatus.resolveIdleServiceStatusView (GpuTierStatus.tsx:200-232) shows the same headline on poll error or missing payload. Failure: no scan running and service scaled to zero -> operator sees an error toast plus a red idle card for a healthy dormant state (CARD-07 succeed quietly). Fix: distinguish dormant/idle from unreachable; toast only when a run is active.
Derive regex only extracts complete ${...} refs; malformed markers like ${PGHOST pass validation and render literally.
fix: Parse derive strictly; reject any $ not starting a well-formed ${NAME} reference.

description: [GAP] The product payload now sends only `name`, while `docs/workbay/contracts/image-description-api.md` still documents `request.context_pack.product` as including name, SKU, and price. The same-slice contract documentation does not reflect the changed outbound data.
fix: Update the owning contract to document name-only product context, or preserve the documented SKU and price fields if their removal was not intended.

description: Underspecified identity resolution: tenants.primary_contact_email is nullable=True (001_identity_schema.py:435) and no recognition/ repository exposes a lookup by email (only customer_provision_service.py writes it). Assumption line 78 'every tenant has a unique primary_contact_email' is not enforced by the schema; behaviour for a Clerk user whose email matches no tenant is undefined.
fix: Plan must add a tenant-by-email lookup (repository method, case-folded), define the response for a verified Clerk email with zero or NULL-email tenant match (distinct 403, no tenant creation), and note that uniqueness on a nullable column does not guarantee every tenant is reachable.
